author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: The world in which we live is a world of imagination. In fact, life itself is an activity of imagining.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Imagining novel solutions to ever more complex problems is far more noble than to run from problems. Life is the continual solution of a continuously synthetic problem.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: To attempt to change circumstances before you change your imaginal activity is to struggle against the very nature of things. There can be no outer change until there is first an imaginal change. Everything you do, unaccompanied by an imaginal change, is but futile readjustment of surfaces.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Whenever one state grows so stable as to become your constant mood, your habitual attitude, then that habitual state defines your character and is a true transformation.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Imagination is both conservative and transformative. It is conservative when it builds its world from images supplied by memory and the evidence of the senses. It is creatively transformative when it imagines things as they ought to be, building its world out of the generous dreams of fancy.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Imagination is spiritual sensation. Enter the image of the wish fulfilled, then give it sensory vividness and tones of reality by mentally acting as you would act were it a physical fact.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Mentally enter into your dream. Mentally do what you would actually do, were it physically true.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: This going into the past and replaying a scene of the past in imagination as it ought to have been played the first time, I call revision — and revision results in repeal.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 1 — The Law: Imagining Creates Reality
quote_original: Live nobly, so that mind can store a past well worthy of recall.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Man, through the medium of a controlled, waking dream, can predetermine his future. That imaginal activity, of living in the feeling of the wish fulfilled, leads man across a bridge of incident to the fulfillment of the dream.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: This ability to mentally move from things as they are to things as they ought to be, is one of the most important discoveries that man can make.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Observe your imaginal activities. Imagine better than the best you know, and create a better world for yourself and others.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Live as though the wish had come, even though it is yet to come, and you will shorten the period of waiting.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Our future is our imaginal activity in its creative march.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: To revise the past is to re-construct it with new content. Man should daily relive the day as he wished he had lived it, revising the scenes to make them conform to his ideals.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: If man does not always create in the full sense of the word, it is because he is not faithful to his vision, or else he thinks of what he wants rather than from his wish fulfilled.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Once we think in terms of influence rather than of clarity of the end desired, the effort of imagination becomes an effort of will, and the great art of imagining is perverted into tyranny.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: To live wisely, we must be aware of our imaginal activities or, at any rate, of the end which they are tending. We must see to it that it is the end we desire. Wise imagining identifies itself only with such activities that are of value or promise well.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: The imaginist dreams while awake. He is not the servant of his Vision, but the master of the direction of his attention.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: But man need not wait for the uprising of new moods in himself; he can create happy moods at will.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: The mood of the wish fulfilled is the high tide which lifts us easily off the bar of the senses where we usually lie stranded.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: It is possible to pass from thinking of to thinking from; but the crucial matter is thinking from, i.e., experiencing the state; for that experience means unification.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Faith plus Love is self-commission. We can’t commit ourselves to what we do not love.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: The shifting of the center of imagining is not brought about by spatial travel but by a change in what we are aware of.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 10 — Things Which Do Not Appear
quote_original: It is for us to assemble the images of happy outcome and then keep from interfering. The event must not be forced but allowed to happen.

author: Neville Goddard
source_section: Chapter 10 — Things Which Do Not Appear
quote_original: It is fatally easy to make the acceptance of the imaginal faith a substitute for living by it.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Out of material others would have thrown away as useless, an awakened imagination refashions it as it ought to be.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: We must imagine we are what we would like to be. We must play it in imagination first — not as a spectator — as an actor.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: It is one thing to think of the end and another thing to think from the end. To think from the end, to enact the end, is to create reality.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Not what the man was, but what he may become should be our imaginal activity.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: There is a wide difference between the will to resist an activity and the decision to change it. He who changes an activity acts; whereas he who resists an activity, re-acts. One creates; the other perpetuates.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Memory, no less than desire, resembles a day-dream. Why make it a daymare?

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: Definition asserts the reality of the particular thing against the formless generalizations which flood the mind.

author: Neville Goddard
quote_original: One real creative moment, one real feeling of the wish fulfilled, is worth more than the whole natural life of re-action.
